files.adapted_why: Same ten stages and the same defaults as the kit (CI_DEFAULT_STAGES is byte-for-byte the kit's value); the divergence is repo-local and additive — a COMPUTO ADAPTATIONS header block recording why the old GTEST_FILTER exclusions, format fallback override and tidy narrowing are gone, a usage() that prints lines 2-22 rather than the derived first blank-line block so that block cannot push the stage list off the screen, a CI_FORMAT_FALLBACK_HEAD knob (the kit always re-checks the last commit when the branch is level with origin/main; here that fallback is switchable, left at the kit's behaviour = 1), CI_VERSION_BINARIES pinned to the CLI binary the version stage must ask, and CI_DEFAULT_STAGES re-stated as a direct assignment so the kit's earlier ${VAR:-...} line cannot silently win. **2026-09-20, card t_45a28893:** the `release` stage was added (an eleventh stage the kit has no counterpart for), with `CI_RELEASE_BUILD_DIR` / `CI_RELEASE_BUILD_TYPE` — every kit stage builds CI_BUILD_TYPE=Debug while the Pages workflow builds Release, so the optimized configuration was checked nowhere locally. It configures, builds, applies the same `warning:` count to its own log and runs the same test command, and its cost is measured in the COMPUTO ADAPTATIONS block (146 s cold, ~5 s on a one-source push). The header's full-tier line also now lists kitprobes and release — it had gone stale on kitprobes when that stage landed. **2026-09-20, card t_4a81d75f:** a twelfth stage, `docs` (no kit counterpart), in CI_DEFAULT_STAGES and in .githooks/pre-push: docs/test-examples.py (all 66 examples, graded against $CI_BUILD_DIR/computo through COMPUTO_BINARY), docs/validate-coverage.py, and docs/LANGUAGE_REFERENCE.md plus both generated indexes held byte-for-byte to what docs/operators.yaml generates (generated into a temp dir, so the stage never rewrites a tracked file). python3 + PyYAML are prerequisites and a missing one FAILS the run instead of SKIPping — the clang stages' SKIP would leave a documentation stage that quietly does nothing, which is the seven-month hole this closes. Measured ~2 s (66 subprocess runs plus three generators). docs/validate-coverage.py also stopped calling a hardcoded `python` (sys.executable now), which is why the stage could not run on this laptop at all.

The kit's knob list with this repo's values filled in plus a COMPUTO OVERRIDES section at the end: CI_VERSION_BINARIES="$CI_BUILD_DIR/computo" (the kit leaves it unset because every project names its binary differently), CI_TEST_CMD and CI_ASAN_TEST_CMD left at the kit's defaults with the two former GTEST_FILTER narrowings documented as removed-because-fixed, and CI_JOBS=4 kept — the kit's own example value, and the one value in this file that does not mirror tools/ci.sh, which defaults to $(nproc). **2026-09-20, card t_45a28893:** `CI_RELEASE_BUILD_DIR` / `CI_RELEASE_BUILD_TYPE` added for the repo-local `release` stage, `CI_DEFAULT_STAGES` documented as the kit's ten plus it, and a paragraph for it in the COMPUTO OVERRIDES section. `cp .ci.env.example .ci.env` is still a no-op: every CI_* variable's effective value was diffed against tools/ci.sh's own defaults with the example sourced — identical, the two new knobs included. **2026-09-20, card t_4a81d75f:** `docs` documented in the overrides section (python3 + PyYAML prerequisite, FAILS instead of skipping, and what the stage grades); no new knob — it reads CI_BUILD_DIR, and `cp .ci.env.example .ci.env` is still a no-op.
